handback.t:
W1 (EMBED-BAKEOFF) is done. The full write-up is `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\g1_board_entry.md`, headed "### VERIFY REQUEST — W1 — G1 EMBED-BAKEOFF", with exact rerun commands, number tables and negatives. Nothing was committed, and Cargo.toml, lib.rs and the rest of src/ are untouched. I did not post a separate interim entry; the one file covers everything.

**Models and security.** I used no new downloads or crates. The only models are the two already audited on disk (py/models/bge-base and the MiniLM from f5), run with the existing onnxruntime. I searched the disk for a bigger embedding model and found none, so none was tested.

**What was built.**
- **Corpus:** a deterministic hard corpus with 240 concepts (30 topics x 8 sibling details that differ in one key detail). Each concept has 2 five-sentence docs, plus 300 off-topic docs. There are 8 queries per concept (clean, typo, terse, chatty) plus 200 off-topic queries. Corpus A uses seed 1; corpus B uses seed 2 with different phrasings and is the fresh confirm corpus.
- **Protocol:** levers tuned on seeds 1-8, held-out seeds 31-60 (corpus A), frozen-pick confirm on corpus B with seeds 61-90. Paired 95% t-CI and Holm throughout.
- **Retrieval bin** (`g1_retrieval`): compares hash, BM25, MiniLM, BGE (with and without the query instruction) and these levers: hybrid BM25 fusion, sentence-chunk max-pool, spell-correct and keyword rewrites, Rocchio pseudo-relevance feedback (PRF), token-overlap rerank, and a MiniLM-to-BGE cascade.
- **Routing bin** (`g1_route`): downstream routing success with a crate-faithful kn-direct+vote policy that accepts any similarity. Worlds are sib16, rand16, sib64, sib16-mixed50 and a no-information control. A ground-truth oracle arm bounds it.
- Both bins are deterministic on rerun except the timing fields. I fixed a HashMap-order float bug in the tf-idf norm along the way.

**Numbers (held-out | fresh corpus B):**
- **Retrieval, BGE vs MiniLM alone:**
  - MRR: +0.020 | +0.023
  - hit@1: +0.026 | +0.035
  - Both are Holm wins; MiniLM hit@1 is .899/.881 and BGE .925/.916.
  - With the query instruction, BGE adds a little more (MRR +0.005 | +0.009 over BGE without it).
  - BM25 hit@1 is .82/.80 and hash is .43; MiniLM beats BM25 by +0.061 | +0.070 MRR.
- **Cost, BGE vs MiniLM:** encode 13.3 ms vs 2.4 ms (5.4x), model 416 MB vs 86 MB (4.8x), vectors about 2x.
- **Routing, BGE vs MiniLM at H2000:** no Holm wins or losses in either split.
  - sib16: -0.012 | -0.007
  - rand16: +0.007 | +0.001
  - MiniLM beats hash by +0.014 to +0.026.
  - A tf-idf cosine ties MiniLM on this corpus.
- **Routing headroom:** the oracle sits about 0.09 to 0.10 above BGE-hybrid, so retrieval quality, not model size, is the limit.
- **MiniLM with system work vs BGE alone, retrieval:** a statistical tie, not a robust win. MiniLM-final (spell-correct plus overlap rerank) vs BGE-alone: MRR +0.003 | +0.004 (not significant after Holm); hit@1 +0.011 (Holm win) | +0.005 (not significant).
- **BGE with the same system:** it still beats MiniLM-final (MRR +0.010 | +0.020, Holm wins).
- **MiniLM + hybrid vs BGE alone, routing (sib16, H2000):** +0.025 (Holm win) | +0.014 (not significant after Holm). This points toward system work beating a bigger model, but is small and not replicated at Holm level.
- **Per-lever effects:**
  - Spell-correct gives nearly all the gain, concentrated in the typo class (hit@1 .77 to .94).
  - Hybrid and rerank add about +0.01, raising top-1 but lowering recall@3 (R@3 .77 to .64 for MiniLM).
  - Chunk max-pool is neutral on MiniLM and -0.013 MRR on BGE.
  - Rocchio PRF is always negative or neutral.
  - Overlap rerank hurts chatty queries.
- **Cascade:** the MiniLM-to-BGE cascade is the best retrieval system (hit@1 .953), but it needs both encoders, so it costs more than BGE alone.
- **Controls:** the knowledge layer loses on the no-information control for every embedder, including the oracle (about -0.02 to -0.03). It is also slightly negative on mixed50, and weak at 64 concepts.

**Verdict.**
1. BGE earns a small retrieval edge (+2 to 3 points hit@1) but does not improve routing outcome.
2. System work on MiniLM roughly ties BGE alone on retrieval at about 1/5 the encode latency; it is not a clean win. It points the same way on routing, but small and unreplicated.
3. Keep MiniLM as the default and add spell-correction. A hybrid dense + tf-idf similarity is worth trying if routing matters. Re-test on real text before changing anything.

**Caveats I flagged in the entry.**
- The corpus is synthetic and templated, with only 3 surface forms per detail, so lexical methods look unrealistically strong.
- The system gain depends on my choice of 25% typo queries; on clean queries the MiniLM system gain is about zero or negative.
- Retrieval CIs are over resampled query subsets of one pool; the A to B replication is the independent check, and it agrees on all signs.
- The routing policy is a replica of the crate's knowledge-router semantics (not the crate itself), and weak-feedback regime W was not run.
- Latencies are from Python onnxruntime on a shared box.

**Disk and repro.** The embedding fixtures and the BGE model add about 110 MB and 416 MB outside src. They are regenerable in about 3.5 minutes per corpus, and you may want to gitignore them. The retrieval and routing bins each take under a minute.
